children: The Allahabad High Court has observed that a finance firm cannot use goons to seize vehicles over loan default and arm a private party with the coercive authority of the state in the process.

The court said a finance company's contractual right to repossess a financed vehicle must be enforced through a forum known to law, such as a civil court or an arbitrator and not by recovery agents who waylay the borrower and seize the vehicle by force.
The court said that reading a repossession clause literally to allow this would arm a private party with the coercive authority of the state.
The court noted that the vehicle of a borrower who had paid 31 of 45 instalments was seized at gunpoint on a highway and the allegation was never specifically denied.

While allowing the writ petition filed by a borrower, Sadab Ahmad, a division bench comprising Justice J J Munir and Justice Indrajeet Shukla directed the vehicle to be delivered forthwith without any precondition, imposed costs of  ₹10,000 and directed the finance company to restructure the loan without penal interest. It left the question of any default open for adjudication by a competent forum.

Passing these directives, the court observed, "The right of the finance company engrafted into a hire-purchase agreement to seize the chattel, the vehicle here, purchased on hire-purchase, gives an enforceable right, no doubt, to the finance company, but that enforcement has to be done through a process known to law. It cannot be done by force employing goons, styled as agents".

"It would be virtually arming a private party with the coercive authority of the state, invariably exercisable by a judge, an arbitrator or some quasi-judicial authority with the aid of its own agency and re-enforced by the police," the court added.
The petitioner, a self-employed man, bought a TATA goods carrier in December 2023 with finance from HDB Financial Services Limited, repayable in 45 instalments of  ₹64,059 each.

On August 9, 2026, men acting for the company allegedly intercepted him at Chandauli, threatened him at gunpoint, took the vehicle and made him sign a repossession inventory, according to the petitioner.
He raised a complaint with the company, the local police and the district magistrate, and then approached the high court, seeking release of the vehicle.

title: Finance firm can't use goons to seize vehicle over loan default: HC
